analysis.title: NeoCloud Bounce Reverses As Operational Risks Rise
key_insights: The neocloud relief bounce reversed Friday Nov 13 as execution and funding concerns resurfaced, including doubts about Nvidia's future capabilities as the 'central bank of AI' after a leadership change. The earnings debate is shifting from a largely set 2027 toward 2028.
CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN were each down more than 9% Friday morning, erasing momentum from the rebound that began earlier in the week on CoreWeave's earnings and better risk appetite toward AI.

Backlog and demand: IREN reported a $20.3 billion backlog and CoreWeave ended 3Q with $132.5 billion. Nebius says customers are signing larger, longer contracts at higher prices and are already asking about 2028 capacity.
Nebius' latest deals cleared above $25 million per megawatt, versus $20-25 million previously.

Customer prepayments are rising. CoreWeave expects about $9 billion of customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. Nebius says prepayments on new contracts cover more than 100% of the associated capex.

Prepayments mean project financing backed by contracted cash flows rather than increasingly expensive borrowing. It does not remove credit risk, but it makes a slowdown in Nvidia's support less of a threat than Thursday's price action implied.
Execution is the more visible constraint. Nebius shares fell after Thursday's results because it pushed some capacity into 2027 due to power and construction delays, not cancellations.
The next phase of the AI capex story is about operational leverage and cash-flow improvements, as companies need to protect margins while growing into future earnings expectations.

ZeroHedge editorial note: a large share of Nvidia's $50-60BN quarterly free cash flow is recycled into customers, suppliers and neoclouds, so even a temporary pause could pull $50BN or more out of the AI ecosystem. ZH compares this to QT for the AI trade, announced by press release at 8:48am.

sector_views.rationale: Demand, backlog and prepayments are strengthening, but Nvidia funding risk and execution delays (power, construction) are driving a sell-off. The focus is moving to operational leverage and cash flow.

earnings_insights: IREN reported a $20.3 billion backlog (reported, 3Q results).
CoreWeave ended 3Q with a $132.5 billion backlog (reported) and expects about $9 billion of customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months (company expectation).

Nebius reported Thursday (Nov 12). It pushed some capacity into 2027 because of power and construction delays. Its latest deals cleared above $25 million per megawatt versus $20-25 million previously, and prepayments on new contracts cover more than 100% of associated capex (company statements).
The earnings debate is shifting beyond a largely set 2027 toward 2028, and customers are already asking Nebius about 2028 capacity.
risk_factors: Funding risk from Nvidia's leadership change, given its outsized role in financing the neocloud ecosystem. A pause in Nvidia's recycling of free cash flow could pull $50BN or more from the AI ecosystem (ZeroHedge estimate).
Execution risk: power and construction delays pushing capacity into 2027, as seen at Nebius.
Credit risk remains even with rising customer prepayments.
Margin pressure as companies need to grow into future earnings expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs are large (CoreWeave $132.5 billion, IREN $20.3 billion), pricing is rising (Nebius above $25 million per megawatt), customers are asking about 2028 capacity, and prepayments (CoreWeave about $9 billion expected, Nebius above 100% of capex) mean contracted-cash-flow financing.
tension_points.bear_case: Nvidia's leadership change raises doubt about its role financing the ecosystem, and a pause could pull $50BN or more out of AI (ZeroHedge). Nebius delayed some capacity into 2027 on power and construction problems.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in Nvidia's support, or further execution delays like Nebius' capacity pushed into 2027.
